title: Blichfeldt's Theorem: k+1 Congruent Points When vol > k

problemStatement.formal: \text{If } S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n \text{ is measurable with } \mathrm{vol}(S) > k, \text{ then } S \text{ contains } k+1 \text{ points with pairwise differences in } \mathbb{Z}^n
problemStatement.plain: Blichfeldt's theorem (1914): any measurable set S in R^n with volume > k contains k+1 distinct points x_1,...,x_{k+1} whose pairwise differences all lie in the integer lattice Z^n. Unlike Minkowski's theorem, no convexity or symmetry is needed.

insights: Iter 23 (researcher-3, 2026-05-14): The `proofs/.lake` recursive self-symlink blocker recorded in every prior state.md/JSON since the original S13 PR (2026-05-08) is **NOT** a Docker blocker. The `docker-build.sh` script overlays a `lean-mathlib-cache` Docker volume at `/workspace/proofs/.lake/build`, which masks the host-side broken symlink chain (`worktree/.lake → main/.lake → self`). Reproducible: `./proofs/scripts/docker-build.sh Proofs.MinkowskiTheoremOQ04` succeeds in ~12 min cold start (Mathlib clone + cache get + build). Prior iterations carrying the .lake blocker forward as a CI gate were over-pessimistic; Docker green build is achievable today, not gated on a separate mechanic infra-repair PR. Generalization: when a state.md carries a `proofs/.lake` infra blocker forward for multiple iterations without actually re-attempting Docker, assume the blocker may have been masked by Docker tooling changes and re-test before deferring.

Iter 23 (researcher-3, 2026-05-14): The S13–S22 "build pending" convention (used by 9 sequential PRs) is safely dischargeable in a single later iteration. Pattern: when a slug has a verified-clean prior baseline (here, S12 era) and subsequent PRs all use the convention "build pending pending mechanic infra repair", a researcher can later run the build themselves and ship a BUILD-VERIFY iteration that retroactively certifies the chain. Cheaper than running CI on each PR; preserves the rapid-iteration value of the convention. Caveat: this only works if (a) Mathlib pin hasn't drifted and (b) no v4.26.0 regressions hit the parent — both true for this slug at this time.

S15 (researcher-12, 2026-05-08): Once an axiom→theorem flip lands in the Lean source but build verification is pending, a useful next-iteration pattern is to add a small downstream-consumer corollary (here, `blichfeldt_three_points` at k=2). Two benefits: (a) **loud regression detection** — if CI exposes a drift bug in the flipped theorem, the corollary fails alongside it, raising the visibility of the failure; (b) **pedagogical demarcation** — a k=2 specialization is the smallest case where the general theorem strictly strengthens iterated k=1, making the increase in expressive power concrete. Cost: 26 lines for a 3-line proof + docstring; risk: zero (corollary depends only on the flipped theorem, no new Mathlib API).

S12 (researcher-11, 2026-05-08): When verifying API names, ALWAYS verify against the project's pinned Mathlib commit (here `2df2f01` = v4.26.0), not master. S11 had verified against master `aac6750`; one name (`Set.Finite.fintype_coe_eq_toFinset_card`) does not exist in either, but might appear stable if the verification source is wrong. The drift fix uses `← Set.toFinset_card` + `simp [hF₀_card]`: `Set.toFinset_card` is `s.toFinset.card = Fintype.card s`, and `(↑F₀ : Set _).toFinset = F₀` follows by simp (with explicit-`have` fallback if simp does not normalize). Pattern: when a verified-master name fails to exist, the recovery is usually a 2-line rewrite that bypasses the missing-name route by going through stable simp lemmas like `Set.toFinset_card` and `Set.toFinset_coe`.

Sorry 1 (ENat/ENNReal cast `(k:ℝ≥0∞)<T.encard ⇒ (k+1:ℕ∞)≤T.encard`): 5 lines via `ENat.toENNReal_lt` (norm_cast) + `ENat.add_one_le_iff (ENat.coe_ne_top k)`. S10 (researcher-12, 2026-05-08): The Path A `tsum-of-indicators → encard` bridge is 2 lines (not 35): `rw [tsum_congr h_summand_eq, ← tsum_subtype, ENNReal.tsum_set_one]`. `tsum_subtype` (used by Mathlib's `Measure.Count.le_count_apply`) provides `∑' _ : ↥s, f _ = ∑' i, s.indicator f i`; combined with `ENNReal.tsum_set_one` (`∑' _ : ↥s, 1 = s.encard`) the covering-count function evaluates to `T(z).encard` where `T(z) := {v : L | (v : ℝⁿ) + z ∈ s}`. Drops Path A line count to ~110 — sharper than S9's 120 estimate.

S10 (researcher-12, 2026-05-08): Path A contrapose unwrap is non-trivial: the goal `∃ pts : Fin (k+1) → ℝⁿ, ...` reformulates cleanly to `∃ z, ∃ vs : Fin (k+1) → L, Injective vs ∧ ∀ i, z + (vs i : ℝⁿ) ∈ s` (factoring out the lattice translation). pts := z + (vs i : ℝⁿ) recovers the original via add_left_cancel + AddSubgroupClass.coe_sub. After contrapose+push_neg, the hypothesis becomes `∀ z, ∀ vs (inj), ∃ i, z + vs i ∉ s`, equivalent to `∀ z, T(z).encard ≤ k` — directly bounded by `setLIntegral_mono_ae`.

S10 (researcher-12, 2026-05-08): Mathlib k=1 → k+1 generalization map: `measure_eq_tsum` → `volume_eq_setLIntegral_indicator_tsum` (proved S9); `measure_iUnion₀` (disjointness ⇒ ∑μ = μ⋃) → Tonelli + pointwise indicator bound (k+1-multiplicity ⇒ ∑ ≤ k); `measure_mono ⋃⊆F` → `setLIntegral_mono_ae c≤k a.e.`. Path A is structurally identical to Mathlib's `exists_pair_mem_lattice_not_disjoint_vadd` 6-line proof, with Tonelli replacing measure_iUnion₀.

S9 (researcher-6, 2026-05-08): Mathlib's own `MeasureTheory.exists_pair_mem_lattice_not_disjoint_vadd` (in `MeasureTheory/Group/GeometryOfNumbers.lean:52`) is the abstract-subgroup form of Blichfeldt's k=1 theorem and uses a 6-line `contrapose!` proof structure (`fund.measure_eq_tsum` → `measure_iUnion₀` → `measure_mono`); mirroring this for the k+1 case avoids the explicit covering-count function and could drop the formalization cost from ≈195 to ≈120 lines. Recommended approach for S10.

S9 (researcher-6, 2026-05-08): The hardest sub-step of the explicit covering-count route is bridging tsum-of-indicator to `Set.ncard` — specifically, `∑' v : L, T.indicator 1 v = (T.ncard : ℝ≥0∞)` (with ⊤ if T infinite). Likely route: `tsum_eq_iSup_sum_of_nonneg` for `ℝ≥0∞` plus Finset.card-of-support reasoning. Estimated 35 lines.

`IsAddFundamentalDomain.exists_ne_zero_vadd_eq` is a one-line proof of Blichfeldt's basic theorem given the standard ℤⁿ-fundamental-domain has volume 1; eliminates the manual partition-pigeonhole pattern and the `blichfeldt_volume_partition` axiom (S8, 2026-05-08).

Half-scaling measurability via preimage rewrite: T = (2:ℝ)⁻¹ • s = ((2:ℝ) • ·) ⁻¹' s; reuses Erdos353Problem inv_smul = preimage bridge; closes with MeasurableSet.preimage + measurable_const_smul.
Half-scaling volume via Measure.addHaar_smul: vol(c • s) = ENNReal.ofReal |c|^(finrank ℝ E) · vol(s). For Fin n → ℝ, finrank = n via Module.finrank_pi + Fintype.card_fin.
ENNReal arithmetic for (1/2)^n · vol(s) > 1 given vol(s) > 2^n: use ENNReal.mul_lt_mul_left with (1/2)^n nonzero and finite, then collapse (1/2)^n · 2^n = 1 via mul_pow + ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel.
Pointwise scoped namespace required: `open Pointwise` (or `open scoped Pointwise`) needed for Set.SMul instance to resolve; Measure.addHaar_smul statement uses pointwise smul on sets.

The Minkowski-Finset clause `↑F ⊆ stdLattice n` is strictly stronger than the Blichfeldt-Finset clause `∀ x y ∈ F, x − y ∈ stdLattice n`: this asymmetry reflects the geometric content of the half-scaling + symmetry + convexity argument that lifts pairwise lattice-difference witnesses to actual lattice-point witnesses. Iter 17 (Blichfeldt-Finset) and Iter 20 (Minkowski-Finset) together expose the Finset-form structural symmetry of the half-scaling bridge.
